name: P25D — the scripted walk must ARRIVE, and must not walk in circles

steps.note:
RUN IT WITH:  node tools/shoot.mjs --keep-title --url http://localhost:8123/index.html --out /tmp/p25d --script scenarios/P25D-loop.json --timeout 300000

THE BUG AS REPORTED, second form: 'the hero walks a loop, back and forth in the cottage, and will not stop'. P25B's recorder only proved the walk SHAPE — y rises gradually, never blocked — and read as green while the boy was going nowhere.

WHAT TO MEASURE. NOT direction changes. A scripted walk that turns a corner changes the sign of its x velocity, and counting those counts every corner in the route — the first version of this scenario reported 5 'reversals' on a walk that was, on inspection, correct: the stair is in the SE corner of the cottage and the loft is in the NE, so the only way up to the chest is round three walls, and two of those walls are corners. A corner is not a loop.

A LOOP IS PATH LENGTH OVER DISPLACEMENT. He covers ground A -> B by the direct route and the quotient is near 1; he goes A -> B -> A -> B and the quotient is whatever the pacing multiplied it by. So the recorder sums every stride and compares it with the straight line from where he started to where he ended. `grind` counts the time he spent moving slower than 0.15 a second, which is what a body being pushed out of a collider looks like from outside.

NOTE ON THE `await`. `__DQ.storyAuto(false)` is asynchronous on purpose — it has to wait for the beat in flight to unwind the stage — and a call that does not await it gets its own beat REFUSED, invisibly, because `storyPlay` settles its promise at the end of a beat rather than at the moment it accepts one. That is not a hypothetical: it is what every version of this scenario did until P25G added `__DQ.storyIssued()` to say so out loud. Read `issued.steps` in the notes below — `1` is this scenario's own walk, `37` is chapter beat b1 walking in from somewhere this run never asked for.
TAKE THE STAGE OFF THE CHAPTER. Not a belt-and-braces skip — this waits, so the beat underneath has actually let go before anything else in the run is measured.

steps.msg: nothing of the chapter's is playing — a staged walk issued into a stage somebody else still holds comes back refused, and the run then measures their beat instead of yours

steps.note:
A WALK THAT CANNOT LOOP, and one that can.

THE LOOPING ONE: across the cottage and up to the chest. Its straight-line displacement is only 7.5 while the legal way round three walls is 19.6, so path-over-displacement reads 2.6 on a CORRECT walk — the detour is the room's shape, not a loop, and a ratio cannot tell those apart. So the number it is judged on is not displacement but ROUTE: the walk must not cover materially more ground than the route the planner gave it, which is 20.2 here. He walked 19.6.

THE FLAT ONE: out of the chair and straight across the room, where there is nothing to walk round and the ratio IS the loop test.

steps.eval: (()=>{__DQ.teleport('hollybank',-3.96,-2.12);window.__r=__DQ.route('at:the chest at the foot of your bed');__DQ.storyPlay([{op:'move',actor:'hero',to:'at:the chest at the foot of your bed',speed:9}]);return JSON.stringify({issued:__DQ.storyIssued(),mark:window.__r.mark,thing:window.__r.thing,end:window.__r.end,routeGround:window.__r.at.ground});})()

steps.msg: the beat that is now playing is THIS scenario's one-step walk — not a chapter beat, which reports its own id and its 37 steps

steps.eval: (()=>{window.__t=[];window.__ti=setInterval(()=>{const p=__DQ.state().player;if(!p)return;const t=performance.now();const row=[p.x,p.y,p.z,t];const P=window.__t[window.__t.length-1];if(P){const dt=Math.max(1,t-P[3])/1000;const v=Math.hypot(p.x-P[0],p.z-P[2])/dt;if(v<0.15)window.__t.grind=(window.__t.grind||0)+dt;}window.__t.push(row);},50);return 'recording strides and grind time';})()

steps.msg: across the cottage and up the stair, he walked no further than the ROUTE he was given: a walk that paces or circles covers ground no route asked for, and the route is known in advance — 20.2 units here, and he covered 19.6
he spent under 3 seconds moving slower than a walk — grinding against furniture is the other face of the same loop, and three corners of a scripted walk are worth about half a second
no walk had to report that it was going nowhere: the stall guard is on PROGRESS, so a walk that keeps closing on its waypoint resets it every frame and a walk that paces never does

steps.note: and now the flat walk, where path-over-displacement IS the test: nothing between the chair and the far wall but floor, so any excess is a loop and nothing else

steps.eval: (()=>{window.__t=[];window.__ti=setInterval(()=>{const p=__DQ.state().player;if(!p)return;const t=performance.now();const row=[p.x,p.y,p.z,t];const P=window.__t[window.__t.length-1];if(P){const dt=Math.max(1,t-P[3])/1000;if(Math.hypot(p.x-P[0],p.z-P[2])/dt<0.15)window.__t.grind=(window.__t.grind||0)+dt;}window.__t.push(row);},50);return 'recording the flat walk';})()

steps.msg: on open floor the walk covered what it crossed: within 1.6x the straight line. This is the loop test proper, on the one leg where a detour has no excuse
and got there without being pushed off anything

steps.note:
THE REGRESSION underneath the loop: the route used to end on the MARK, which for every chest and every table is inside a collider. The boy was told to walk to a place he could never stand, so the only way the step could end was its clock — reporting failure while the beat carried on. The route now ends on a tile his body fits on, near the mark.

WHICH MARK, THOUGH. The mark is an internal mark: the chest plus a deliberate 0.96 offset out of its own collider, and then pushed to the first spot the body fits. So "how far from the mark did he stop" is a number about the planner's scaffolding that no player could check. The chest's position is JITTERED between runs as well, so the honest question is the one a player asks — is he close enough to OPEN it — answered against the chest itself, whose reach the beat uses to search it. `__DQ.route` reports the thing it resolved for exactly this: `describe()` replaces every array with a count, so a chest's position is otherwise unreadable from here.

steps.eval: (()=>{__DQ.teleport('hollybank',-3.96,-2.12);const r=__DQ.route('at:the chest at the foot of your bed');window.__r=r;__DQ.storyPlay([{op:'move',actor:'hero',to:'at:the chest at the foot of your bed',speed:9}]);return JSON.stringify({issued:__DQ.storyIssued(),mark:r.mark,thing:r.thing,end:r.end,routeAt:r.at});})()

steps.msg: the scripted chest walk ends UP on the loft, at the chest's own floor
and ends within the chest's own reach of the chest — close enough to open it, which is the question a player asks and the only one the mark cannot answer
he got there without stalling: a route that ends inside furniture paces the last few centimetres until the step's clock runs out

steps.note: and the same walk again from the other side of the room, because a pathfinder that only works from one starting tile is a pathfinder with a lucky seed

steps.eval: (()=>{__DQ.teleport('hollybank',-4.5,1.5);const r=__DQ.route('at:the chest at the foot of your bed');window.__r=r;__DQ.storyPlay([{op:'move',actor:'hero',to:'at:the chest at the foot of your bed',speed:9}]);return JSON.stringify({issued:__DQ.storyIssued(),chest:r.thing,end:r.end});})()

steps.msg: the same walk from the other corner of the cottage also arrives in reach of the chest
and from there too, it ends up on the loft rather than under it
